written.myAnswer: In dynamic equilibrium, forward and reverse changes continue at equal rates. In static equilibrium, there is no change or movement.

An irreversible reaction proceeds only in the forward direction under the given conditions, while a reversible reaction proceeds in both directions because its products can form the reactants again under the same conditions.

Combustion reactions release a large amount of heat and form products that do not readily react to reform the original reactants under the same conditions; therefore, they proceed effectively in the forward direction.

Changing conditions can make a reaction reversible if its products can then react to form the reactants. A reversible reaction can be driven to completion by removing a product, such as allowing a gaseous product to escape.
A reversible reaction proceeds in both directions under the same conditions and is represented by ⇌. An irreversible reaction proceeds only in the forward direction and is represented by →.
These phase changes are reversible: ice melts to liquid water and liquid water freezes to ice; liquid water evaporates to vapour and vapour condenses to liquid water.
A reversible reaction can be driven to completion by removing one of its products from the reaction mixture, including by allowing a gaseous product to escape.

Copper sulphate pentahydrate is blue because it contains water of crystallisation. Heating removes the water and forms white anhydrous copper sulphate. The change is reversible: the anhydrous salt absorbs moisture and turns blue again.
